scope: Educational planet explorer. The mission files are retained as an archive and are not part of the current planet-only interface.

body_data.origin: Imported bilingual descriptions and NASA Planetary Fact Sheet references from the original demo.
body_data.verification: Schema and physical ranges are checked automatically. The complete narrative and all physical values have not been independently re-verified.
body_data.visual_model: Planet radii, distances, orbits and animation speeds are illustrative; this is not a scientific ephemeris.

archival_mission_data.origin: Imported mission records from the original demo. Most original sources are textual references rather than direct URLs.
archival_mission_data.date_convention: Dates are historical calendar dates as imported; some Chinese launches use Beijing calendar dates while others use UTC. They are not precise comparable timestamps.
archival_mission_data.active_definition: An imported operating-status snapshot, not proof that a spacecraft is presently communicating. Being in orbit is not the same as operational.
archival_mission_data.unknown_end_dates: An inactive record with null end_date means that the exact end date is unverified, never an ongoing mission.
archival_mission_data.review_metadata: reviewed_on records a targeted check only. verified_fields identifies the fields checked against source_urls; other fields retain their original provenance.
archival_mission_data.name_collisions: Genesis and Beresheet both use the Chinese name 创世纪号. Distinct IDs must be preserved; translated names cannot be used for deduplication.
archival_mission_data.pending: The full archive, current active statuses, dates and multilingual summaries require a dedicated source audit before scientific or live-status use.
